root_causes.description: product-catalog, a leaf service with no downstream dependencies, exhibited a massive p99 latency spike (~9.6s vs ~2-10ms for healthy peer leaf services) with zero errors, flat CPU (0.011 cores), flat memory (~23.7MB), and zero pod restarts — a pure latency fault (added delay/wait, not resource-bound). All three of its callers (checkout, frontend, recommendation) inherited the latency, while services that do not depend on product-catalog (cart, payment, currency, email, shipping, ad) stayed at ~2-5ms, confirming product-catalog as the single origin.

evidence.observed_value: product-catalog p99_latency_ms=9600.384, max=10000.0 (anomaly flagged); peer leaf services: cart p99=3.88ms, payment/currency/shipping/ad p99=1.98ms
evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms < 10ms for leaf services (cart=3.88ms, payment=1.98ms observed in same window)

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.011, p99=0.012, max=0.012 cores — flat, no anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: no CPU spike — rules out cpu_stress as the cause

evidence.observed_value: memory mean=23760896 bytes, max=23904256 bytes — flat, no anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: no memory growth — rules out memory_stress

evidence.observed_value: user_checkout_single trace, 16246ms, status ok (0 errors); search_traces on product-catalog with min_duration_ms=3000 returned 20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=39521ms
evidence.expected_baseline: traces normally complete in <100ms with 0 errors — slow-but-successful spans confirm latency fault, not http_abort

evidence.query_or_id: Updated: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource (count=1)
evidence.observed_value: only pod event for product-catalog in window — no OOMKilled, BackOff, or FailedMount
evidence.expected_baseline: no crash-loop events expected for a healthy pod

evidence.observed_value: [no logs found] — no error/slow/timeout log lines during the window
evidence.expected_baseline: no error logs — consistent with silent added latency rather than an exception path

root_causes.description: checkout's p99 latency spiked to ~9.4s (vs p50 of ~25ms) purely as propagation from its downstream dependency product-catalog; its own CPU was flat (0.002 cores), error rate was 0, and its other dependencies (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency) were all healthy, so the latency is inherited, not self-inflicted.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms ~25ms (p50 baseline observed in same window)

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.002, p99=0.003, max=0.003 cores — flat, no anomaly detected
evidence.expected_baseline: no CPU spike — checkout itself is not compute-stressed; latency inherited from product-catalog dependency

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.0 for all services including checkout throughout the window
evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01 — no error spike, ruling out http_abort/dependency failure errors

root_causes.description: frontend, the user-facing entry point, showed p99 ~9.6s (vs p50 ~25ms) with zero errors — fully explained by propagation: per the service topology, frontend calls checkout, recommendation, and product-catalog directly, all three of which were slow due to product-catalog, while its other dependencies (cart, shipping, currency, ad) were healthy.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms ~25ms (p50 baseline observed in same window)
error_rate < 0.01 — latency-only incident, no failed requests

evidence.observed_value: user_browse_product trace, 5403ms, status ok; search_traces on frontend with min_duration_ms=3000 returned 20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=39521ms

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog for an injected/artificial delay (e.g., a flagd feature flag or chaos experiment adding sleep to request handlers) and disable it — flat CPU (0.011 cores) with 10s p99 indicates waiting, not compute
Profile product-catalog request handlers for blocking sleeps, lock contention, or slow datastore/gRPC calls if no fault flag is found
Add strict client timeouts and circuit breakers on product-catalog calls from checkout, frontend, and recommendation so a slow catalog cannot propagate ~10s latencies into user-facing checkout flows
Configure a p99 latency SLO alert on product-catalog (e.g., p99 > 500ms for 2 minutes) to detect recurrence before it degrades frontend/checkout
